evidence.quote: Leaves can be harvested after plants grow 1.5– 2.0 m, which usually takes 6 to 12 months after planting depending on the growth conditions
evidence.doc: North West Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, Moringa (Moringa oleifera) production: A possible solution to South African food security challenges

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: The 6–12-month reference concerns the first leaf harvest after planting. Flowers and pods are normally produced during the second year of growth in the same North West guide. Leaf readiness does not establish pod production or picking months.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Not found in any fetched SA source. Mabapa et al. (2017) state 'Farmers have no idea of leaf yield'.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Not found per plant. The North West DARD guide gives only '20 metric tons of moringa pods per hectare per year' with no plant density, so a per-plant figure would be a derivation and is not made.

chillUnits.notes: No chill requirement figure found. North West DARD guide: tolerates light frost; the same guide recommends Bojanala because of non-occurrence of frost in winter.

pollination.notes: No statement about self-fertility found in a fetched SA source. North West DARD guide only says honey bees are the dominant pollinators (not sufficient to assign a union value).

supplementaryReferences.title: Pod development, not a young green-pod picking calendar
supplementaryReferences.quote: Fruits production mainly occurs in March and April.
supplementaryReferences.doc: North West Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, Moringa (Moringa oleifera) production: A possible solution to South African food security challenges
supplementaryReferences.note: This botanical description discusses pods that become brown at maturity. The separate harvesting section requires young, tender, green pods for food and supplies no calendar for that stage. March–April is retained as pod-development phenology, not a confirmed young-pod picking season or leaf calendar.

gaps: Leaf-harvest months not sourced: Mabapa et al. (2017) report SA farmers 'harvest the tree foliage when necessary' and plant 'throughout the year except during winter' (no months given). Heliyon 2024 (Limpopo) gives only frequency: 'The leaves were harvested 4 - 9 times in a year'. No leaf window is shipped.

Exact young green-pod picking months are not stated. The former March–April bar was withdrawn in the 11 October 2026 stage audit because the source dates fruit production rather than the young, tender, green food stage; the observation remains supplementary phenology.
Years to full bearing, per-plant yield, chill and pollination behaviour: no fetched SA source.
Mabapa et al. (2017, Int. J. Agron., Wiley), MDPI Pretoria 2025 paper, jarts.info paper and the DALRRD moringa brochure were blocked or contained no months.
NEMBA 2020: Moringa is not listed (checked GN 1003 of 18 Sept 2020) so 'none'.
